KIGALI – The race for places at the 2026 NCBA Golf Series grand finale in Nairobi began at Kigali Golf Resort & Villas on Saturday, October 17, with golfers completing the opening round of a two-day qualifier that will determine who advances to the regional showdown.

The first day produced a competitive leaderboard across the different handicap categories, with players now facing a second round scheduled for next weekend.

At the end of the two days, the top three players in each category will earn places at the grand finale, scheduled for November 27 at Karen Country Club in Kenya.

Philip Jacob Mavelil led the Men’s 0–9 category with a net score of 70, while Benjamin Mukisa and Evans Mose followed on 71.

In the Men’s 10–18 division, Sibo Gahakwa Frank took the early lead with a net 65, followed by Jesh Tugume, Eugene Munyaneza, Janvier Gasasira and Aditya Chacko, who each returned net scores of 70.

Peter Nizeyimana set the pace in the Men’s 19–28 category with a net 64, ahead of Park Sangyoul on 66 and John Nsibirwa on 71.

The ladies’ divisions also produced strong opening performances. Olivia Ntambara led the Ladies’ 0–18 category with a net 70, followed by Mary Maina on 73 and Alice Rwigema on 74.

In the Ladies’ 19–36 division, Gloriose Uwanyirigira topped the leaderboard with a net 70, ahead of Eva Blaise Zigiriza on 73 and Pacifique Linda Ikirezi on 76.

In the seniors’ category, Park Sunran led with a net 65, while Innocent Rutamu returned 69 and Joseph Ntambara 71.

The standings remain provisional, leaving players another opportunity to improve their positions when competition resumes next weekend.

The Kigali qualifier brought together golfers from different backgrounds, reinforcing the tournament’s role as both a competitive platform and a meeting point for Rwanda’s golfing community.

NCBA Bank Rwanda Managing Director Maurice Toroitich also took part in the competition, reflecting the bank’s involvement beyond its role as tournament sponsor.

Through its “Conquer the Course” theme, the NCBA Golf Series promotes competition, personal achievement and the pursuit of excellence while creating opportunities for participants to build professional relationships.

Golf offers a distinctive setting for such connections, bringing business leaders, professionals and other enthusiasts together around a shared interest. The series uses that appeal to connect players across East Africa while encouraging greater participation in the sport.

The Kigali event also follows the NCBA Junior Golf Tournament held in July, extending the bank’s support across different stages of the game.

While junior tournaments give young players opportunities to develop their skills and gain competitive experience, the adult series allows established golfers to test their abilities against a wider field.

Launched in 2021, the NCBA Golf Series was established to identify golfing talent, encourage healthy competition and strengthen personal and professional networks.

Its expansion beyond Kenya to Rwanda, Uganda and Tanzania has created a regional platform through which golfers can compete and connect across national borders.

With one round completed, attention now shifts to next weekend, when the Kigali players return to the course for the decisive second day. The opening scores have established early leaders, but the remaining round leaves room for the standings to change.

Players near the top will need to protect their positions, while those further down the leaderboard have another opportunity to close the gap and secure a place among the three qualifiers in their respective categories.

The leading players will represent their categories at the NCBA Golf Series grand finale at Karen Country Club on November 27, bringing Rwanda’s qualifiers into competition with players advancing from across the region.

The series combines sporting competition with a wider commitment to developing golf and strengthening connections across East Africa.

For the players, next weekend offers the final opportunity to turn their opening-round performances into a place at the regional finale. The first day has set the pace. The decisive round is still to come.

KIGALI – Rwanda’s dream of reaching the CECAFA U-17 Championship final ended in heart break after Somalia prevailed 5-4 on penalties following a 1-1 draw in a tense semi-final that left the hosts with little to show for a spirited performance.

The junior Amavubi had fought their way into the contest, taken the lead through substitute Patrick Ujeneza and looked capable of securing a place in the final.

But Somalia captain Mohamud Osman equalized just five minutes later, and neither side could find a decisive goal before the match was settled from the spot.

Rwanda came out looking for an early breakthrough with Kevin Munyembaraga rising to meet a cross with a header that sailed inches over the crossbar in the opening minutes.

The match soon developed into a closely fought contest, with Somalia also threatening.

Rwanda’s goalkeeper was called into action in the 23rd and 24th minutes, making important saves as the visitors looked to take advantage of their attacking pressure. The teams went into half-time locked at 0-0.

The breakthrough finally came 18 minutes into the second half, when Ujeneza produced one of Rwanda’s most memorable moments of the match.

The substitute dribbled past three Somalia players before placing the ball into the bottom-right corner, sending the home supporters into celebration.

But Rwanda’s advantage lasted only five minutes when Osman restored parity for Somalia with a goal of his own, bringing the match back to life and forcing the hosts to find another route to the final.

Both sides became more cautious as the contest tightened, but Rwanda continued to search for a winner.

Ezekiel Tuyishimire, who had replaced Pacifique Bahati, nearly made an impact after receiving a through-ball from Ujeneza. Zaidi Niyonzima also came close, sending a strike narrowly wide in the 75th minute.

With neither team able to break the deadlock, penalties would decide which side advanced.

Rwanda converted through Heylen Jeyden Shema and Khalifa Shyaka, while Niyonzima also found the net.

However, missed attempts kept the hosts under pressure in a shootout that Somalia eventually won 5-4.

Rwanda’s goalkeeper managed to save one of Somalia’s penalties, while Asad Mohamed struck the foot of the post, but those reprieves were not enough to spare the hosts elimination.

Uganda’s First-Half Blitz Secures Final Place

In the other semi-final, Uganda booked their place in the final after overwhelming Ethiopia with four first-half goals.

Arnold Kayemba and Ukashsa Jemba scored in the opening minutes to give Uganda a 2-0 lead. Yusuf Ssenyonga then struck twice, scoring in the 32nd and 38th minutes to put Uganda firmly in control at the break.

Ethiopia responded with greater urgency after half-time, creating several opportunities and forcing Uganda’s goalkeeper into important saves, including an intervention in a one-on-one situation.

However, Uganda held on to their advantage to secure victory. The result sets up a final between Uganda and Somalia, while Rwanda’s campaign ends one step short of the title decider.

The junior wasps will meet Ethiopia on Monday October 19, to decide the third place winner who will join the two finalists at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) to be held in Morocco in April and May 2027.

For the hosts, a couple of brilliant goals and a determined performance offered moments of promise, but the decisive penalty miss on Saturday left their final ambitions in ruins.
